Flood Insurance Data

How often do NFIP flood claims get paid?

Of 267,655 NFIP flood claims for losses from 2020 on, 83.4% had a recorded payment. In the 68 counties with 500 or more such claims, the share runs from 52.7% in Terrebonne Parish, LA to 94.4% in Somerset County, NJ.

83.4%
Claims with a recorded payment, U.S., losses 2020 on
267,655
NFIP claims counted

FEMA OpenFEMA NFIP Claims v3, as of August 31, 2026. A recorded payment is any building, contents or Increased Cost of Compliance payment above $0. Left out: 15,151 records FEMA coded "Claim deleted in error" or "Assigned in error"; counted as claims with no payment, the U.S. share would be 79.0%. FEMA's data does not say whether a claim is still open, so a recent claim with no payment may still be paid.

What these numbers cannot tell you

No recorded payment does not mean a claim was denied: it includes damage under the deductible, claims not pursued and reasons FEMA does not record. These are shares of claims filed, not a chance that any one claim gets paid.
